title: Commercial Cleaning Contracts — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: From a sub-$1,000 launch to six-figure accounts: lean founder playbooks, first-contract walkthroughs and proposals, cold-call and paid-search prospecting, production-rate bid math, stress-tested worked bids, and the proof packages that win day porter, medical, and big-client contracts

worksheets.title: Lean Launch and First Contract Planner
worksheets.purpose: Map a lean launch budget, a first-week calling plan, and the walkthrough-to-close sequence that wins the first recurring contract on dependability and speed, priced from day one for the labor the account will eventually need.
instructions: Separate every launch expense into buy-now and defer-until-close columns before spending a single dollar on supplies or insurance.
Set a daily calling target and project the walkthroughs and contracts that volume should produce over the first thirty days.
Price the first account for hired labor, not for your own time, and confirm worker classification before any helper starts.
Arrive early to every walkthrough, measure only cleanable square footage, and qualify the prospect on pain, decision, and budget.
Send the proposal within two to three hours of the walkthrough and expand only when current accounts run smoothly.

fields.name: launch_budget_ledger
fields.prompt: List every dollar you will spend before your first signed contract, separating items you must buy now from items you will defer until a deal closes, such as supplies and insurance. Write the total and confirm it stays under your launch ceiling.
fields.example: Buy now: $99 CBN membership, about $200 for the LLC, and a $25 domain, roughly $324 against a $1,000 ceiling [AJ SIMMONS — VrlDbQP4iQI @ 00:14:20]. Defer: zero cleaning supplies until a deal closes. Insurance is quoted today but purchased only when a deal is ready to close [AJ SIMMONS — VrlDbQP4iQI @ 00:15:12].

fields.name: week_one_call_plan
fields.prompt: Write your first-week calling target, the daily dial count Monday through Friday, and the walkthroughs you expect from that volume. Then project how many additional calls it will take to convert those walkthroughs into recurring contracts and monthly revenue.
fields.example: Target 400 calls in week one, projecting one to four walkthroughs. Another 1,500 calls should yield one to four contracts worth about $2K a month recurring [AJ SIMMONS — VrlDbQP4iQI @ 00:14:20]. 100 calls a day means 2,000 a month, 10-20 appointments and at least 1-2 closes [AJ SIMMONS — ZDdd0TDbbFo @ 00:03:56].

fields.name: hands_on_vs_hire_decision
fields.prompt: Decide whether you will clean the first accounts yourself or hire from day one, and explain why. Note which tasks you must personally learn before delegating and the point at which a helper takes over the account.
fields.example: I will clean the gym account myself for the first months, because 'you have to do everything yourself first' [AJ SIMMONS — 7pVd69Als0I @ 00:00:57]. Counterpoint logged: AJ also says 'Hire people from day one' [AJ SIMMONS — srB5UatlJlU @ 00:16:38]. Compromise: I work alongside the first helper, then step back once the checklist runs without me.

fields.name: labor_priced_rate
fields.prompt: State the monthly price for your first account and show it covers the labor you will eventually hire, not just your own time. Record the wage you assume, the expected labor share, and the net margin you are protecting.
fields.example: Priced the gymnastics facility 'to have employees in there' from the first invoice [DJ The Boss — ZVDOV6jG8Dw @ 00:09:55]. Benchmark split: labor 60%, supplies 10%, marketing and operations 10%, net 15-20% [UpFlip — d4Iip7BHXwg @ 00:08:13]. If my quote only works while I personally clean, it fails the gate and gets repriced before sending.

fields.name: worker_classification_check
fields.prompt: Name the accountant or bookkeeper who will confirm how your first helper is classified, the date of that conversation, and the classification decided. This must be settled before the helper works a single shift on any account.
fields.example: Booked a call with our bookkeeper before the first helper starts on the gym account, because one operator paid a $12,000 misclassification fine [UpFlip — d4Iip7BHXwg @ 00:24:43]. Decision recorded in writing with the date. If the bookkeeper cannot confirm the classification in time, the helper's start date moves; I cover the shifts until it is settled.

fields.name: prospect_list_source
fields.prompt: Build a qualified prospect list and describe where each name came from, such as Google Maps, referrals, or a networking group. Write the number of qualified prospects, the filter you used, and the first referral channel you will join.
fields.example: Pulled 50 qualified offices from Google Maps, since 50 qualified prospects beat hundreds of random calls [Janitorial Empire — 8ireVJkHvoo @ 00:02:03]. Referral channel: a BNI group of 15 to 30 people, doing the one-to-ones and expecting 3 to 4 offices [Mike Mak — G2qoM4LqGdM @ 00:04:46]. Every name gets a source tag on the list.

fields.name: walkthrough_observation_notes
fields.prompt: Record what you observed during the walkthrough, starting with the lobby wait. List the dust, smudges, and fixture details you checked, your laser-measured cleanable square footage, and any test the point of contact set for you.
fields.example: Arrived 20 minutes early; lobby showed cobwebs, ledge dust, floor smudges and window fingerprints [AJ SIMMONS — IMsJ1NxKfUk @ 00:04:13]. Checked partition ledges, blinds and toilet bolts when the manager tested me [AJ SIMMONS — Xvc-7yo1lng @ 00:05:39]. Laser-measured cleanable space only, skipping storage, so the bid does not run way too high [AJ SIMMONS — mk-8avM72Ms @ 00:02:52].

fields.name: qualification_and_pain
fields.prompt: Write the prospect's answers to the three qualifiers of pain, decision, and budget. Identify who signs, what frustrates them about the current cleaner, and the number you will float if the budget conversation stalls before the proposal stage.
fields.example: Pain: the current vendor skips restroom restocking. Decision: the office manager influences, the owner signs. Budget: stalled, so I floated a number 25-30% higher, per the three qualifiers of pain, decision and budget [OctoClean Media — 1tf8JMWxi98 @ 00:00:44]. Because a cleaner is already in place, I offered a complimentary quote 'on file' [AJ SIMMONS — ZDdd0TDbbFo @ 00:05:20].

fields.name: proposal_turnaround_and_contents
fields.prompt: Log the time the walkthrough ended and the time the proposal was sent. List the sections included, covering facility understanding, your systems, the scope, security procedures, and the work-order rule for extras, so it can be forwarded upward.
fields.example: Walkthrough ended 10:15, proposal sent 12:40, inside the two-to-three-hour gate [AJ SIMMONS — QBuGc_Q36dg @ 00:05:39]. Sections: facility understanding, systems, defined scope [OctoClean Media — OzSRs5osKKI @ 00:01:34]; alarm, locks, lights and calling-security steps, since silence on security cost a $50,000-a-year account [Cleaning Launch — V84a_KWRYU4 @ 00:07:28]. Written to stand alone when forwarded.

fields.name: close_terms_and_onboarding
fields.prompt: Record the closing terms you secured, including payment timing, contract length, and references offered. Then list the onboarding steps for the first two weeks and the condition that must be true before you pursue the next account.
fields.example: Closed a 12-month agreement on net 15 after asking for upfront payment [AJ SIMMONS — VrlDbQP4iQI @ 00:16:03]. Closed with references instead of pricing a scope of work [AJ SIMMONS — QBuGc_Q36dg @ 00:04:54]. Onboarding: keys, alarm codes, supply closet, first-week check-in. Next account waits until current accounts run smoothly [ONLY MAIDS PODCAST — aQj7G__L-iE @ 00:23:04].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete when launch spending stays under the ceiling with supplies and insurance deferred, the first price covers hired labor, classification is confirmed in writing, and the proposal left within three hours of the walkthrough.

worksheets.title: Prospecting Engine and Production-Rate Bid Builder
worksheets.purpose: Design the outreach machine that opens doors through cold calls, cold email, in-person visits, and paid search, then convert each qualified walkthrough into a labor-hour bid built on tested production rates and an honest bill rate.
instructions: Script every opener so it leads with a neighbor reference and asks only for a walkthrough or permission to follow up.
Set dial volume, email caps, and paid-search guardrails in writing before any outreach begins or any ad dollar is spent.
Collect cleanable square footage, not building totals, and use headcount when the prospect cannot give the number.
Convert footage into hours with your own tested production rate, then multiply by visits, 52 weeks, and divide by 12.
Never shrink the honest labor estimate to look competitive; load every real cost before the price leaves your hands.

fields.name: call_opener_script
fields.prompt: Write your cold-call opener word for word. Remove any line that leads with your name, company name, or services, and replace it with a neighbor reference. State the single ask of the call, which must be a walkthrough or follow-up permission.
fields.example: Opener: 'We just started serving that facility next door,' before any name, because buildings take hundreds of calls a day [Commercial Cleaning CEO — f9f6YA_kX78 @ 00:00:55]. 'Can I speak to the person in charge of your janitorial services, would you be open to us coming out and giving you a quote' [Jeremy Dixon — -LFfJivPXKw @ 00:02:41]. No price over the phone.

fields.name: dial_volume_and_dialer
fields.prompt: Set the daily dial target and name who makes the calls, you or a trained setter. Write the expected funnel from 100 calls down to walkthroughs, and state the close rate you need to reach your yearly contract goal.
fields.example: Owner dials 50 a day now, the top of the 20-50 range, against 250-400 for a trained setter [Anton Pantio — -1k_o5iWj8w @ 00:08:12]. Funnel: 100 calls, 20-30 reached, 10-15 conversations, 3-5 qualified, 1-2 walkthroughs; 8 walkthroughs a month at 25% equals 2 contracts monthly, 24 a year [Carolyn Arellano — xJ6TUBTc4Qo @ 00:03:26].

fields.name: number_screening_and_location
fields.prompt: Describe how you screen phone numbers before dialing and what you say when a prospect asks where you are based. Note which number patterns you skip, which you call direct, and how the answer keeps the conversation local.
fields.example: Skip 844 and 1-800 numbers because they route into a call tree; dial local 303-style numbers, which signal a privately owned business [The Profitable Cleaner — u3njpVGKi3M @ 00:12:01]. When asked where we are based, answer with the prospect's own city, the way Linton's setters do across about 90 served cities [Daniel Linton — B415KkGunUw @ 00:09:39].

fields.name: cold_email_sequence
fields.prompt: Outline your cold email sequence, including the list source, the sending tool, the number of emails, and the daily send volume. Note the seasonal angle you will use and the safeguard that keeps your sending domain off blacklists.
fields.example: Four-email property manager sequence built with Lemlist plus D7 Lead Finder; a December send asks to 'quote for 2025' because December is slow for property managers [Constantin Schröck — Q5K2zTuisJc @ 00:04:22]. That campaign drew 8 positive replies [Constantin Schröck — Q5K2zTuisJc @ 00:00:00]. Capped daily volume well below 1,000, never from Gmail [Commercial Cleaning CEO — esIqvQsbxco @ 00:15:55].

fields.name: paid_search_guardrails
fields.prompt: Set your Google Ads guardrails before spending a dollar. Record the daily budget, the target cost per conversion, the target conversion rate, and the rule for when you raise spend, so the platform never controls your money.
fields.example: Daily budget $100; targets of $60-70 per conversion at a 20-25% rate, benchmarked against a janitorial account that ran $95 per conversion at 24% [Clicks Geek — EuwGlvViI4w @ 00:01:28]. Raise spend only $25 a week while both numbers hold [Clicks Geek — EuwGlvViI4w @ 00:03:10]. Rule: 'don't give Google the power to go spend your money' [Commercial Cleaning CEO — esIqvQsbxco @ 00:12:04].

fields.name: property_manager_access
fields.prompt: Name the route you will use to reach property managers who rarely answer cold calls, such as trade groups, email, or in-person visits. Write the specific group or site, the meeting cadence, and the first introduction you plan to request.
fields.example: Join IFMA, the trade group The Profitable Cleaner's property-manager guest pointed to. In person: pull up on construction trailers at 5 to 6 AM to catch project managers and general contractors, the way Charles Banks fed post-construction work [AJ SIMMONS — du4OAGZv9AE @ 00:15:26]. Talk to the right people and reference neighbors [Commercial Cleaning CEO — wC3VDZWQwZk @ 00:13:12].

fields.name: cleanable_square_footage
fields.prompt: Record the cleanable square footage, not the building total, and how you obtained it. If the prospect did not know it, show the headcount estimate you used and whether the job clears your in-house minimum bid.
fields.example: Prospect quoted building square footage; I asked for cleanable space, remembering the 655,000 sq ft claim that held an 823 sq ft office [OctoClean Media — zAGjNnpTUcY @ 00:17:52]. Headcount: 20 employees at about 200 cleanable sq ft each, roughly 4,000 sq ft [OctoClean Media — zAGjNnpTUcY @ 00:18:31]. Weekly service, so the in-house minimum price applies [AJ SIMMONS — vqE3IAR7B18 @ 00:12:18].

fields.name: production_rate_hours
fields.prompt: Convert cleanable square footage into labor hours using a production rate you have tested on your own crews. Show the rate, the hours per visit, the visit count, and the monthly hours after multiplying by 52 and dividing by 12.
fields.example: 4,000 cleanable sq ft at a tested 3,500 sq ft per hour equals about 1.14 hours per visit, inside the 3,500-4,000 office band [ONLY MAIDS PODCAST — aQj7G__L-iE @ 00:05:57]. Five visits a week times 52, divided by 12, gives roughly 24.7 hours a month [OctoClean Media — SXNq_81x8SY @ 00:05:48]. Walk time is priced separately [ISSA Media — nBB03PNbUHI @ 00:06:03].

fields.name: bill_rate_and_split
fields.prompt: Set your hourly bill rate from the going wage for incoming janitors in your territory, not the legal minimum. Show the multiplier, the monthly base, the supply charge, and how the result lands against a forty-thirty-thirty cost split.
fields.example: Going rate for incoming janitors here is $15, so doubling gives a $30 bill rate [AJ SIMMONS — 7VHAkhs_HG4 @ 00:02:48]. 24.7 hours at $30 is $741, plus 3% supplies, about $22, for roughly $763 [Carolyn Arellano — IJlyq2UAXqU @ 00:06:05]. Labor lands near 49%, above the 40/30/30 target, so I revisit the rate [7 Figure Cleaning — 1_z-Kgj0GYM @ 00:01:17].

fields.name: honest_estimate_check
fields.prompt: Compare your honest labor estimate against the price you are tempted to send. Record whether you trimmed hours to look competitive, the square-foot cross-check figure if you ran one, and the final number you will defend.
fields.example: Honest estimate is five hours a visit; I refused to present three, because 'the work doesn't disappear because you lowered your price' [Clean Ops Guide — 9ojOIxznBUc @ 00:06:46]. Cross-check at 19-20 cents per foot, then met in the middle [Darian Jarrett — QlIScHN-MPE @ 00:00:15]. Loaded back office, transportation, churn and overtime first [OctoClean Media — cVCpNgEj_zc @ 00:06:12].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete when the opener leads with a neighbor reference, dial and ad guardrails are written, cleanable footage is confirmed, and the bid shows tested production hours, a market-based bill rate, and an unshrunk labor estimate.

worksheets.title: Worked Bid Calculator and Big-Account Readiness Sheet
worksheets.purpose: Run a full worked bid from fixture counts to a stress-tested monthly price, protect cash flow through slow payment terms, and assemble the niche selection, day porter math, and low-risk proof package that big clients require.
instructions: Count fixtures as individual units and subtract walls and fixed furniture from measured footage before applying any production rate.
Load the base wage with every payroll liability, then build full cost line by line including forgotten site tasks.
Divide full cost by one minus the target margin, price weekly service at 4.33 weeks, and stress-test one extra hour.
Bank one month of account costs before pursuing the next contract, because slow terms push payment toward day 60.
Choose a stable niche, confirm the porter bill rate clears wage plus load, and package proof that makes you look safe.

fields.name: fixture_and_area_count
fields.prompt: Inventory every fixture and surface before pricing, counting toilets, urinals, and sinks as individual units rather than rooms. Record each flooring type, the measured square footage, and the deduction you applied for walls and fixed furniture on this site.
fields.example: Counted 6 toilets, 2 urinals and 5 sinks as units, not two bathrooms, since units are what take time [Commercial Cleaning CEO — IMbK5m7qbY0 @ 00:07:02]. Flooring: carpet offices, VCT break room, tile restrooms [ISSA Media — nBB03PNbUHI @ 00:05:11]. Measured 12,000 sq ft, subtracted 15% for walls and furniture, leaving 10,200 cleanable [Commercial Cleaning CEO — IMbK5m7qbY0 @ 00:10:01].

fields.name: loaded_labor_rate
fields.prompt: Calculate the true hourly cost of each cleaner by stacking payroll liabilities on the base wage. List unemployment, FICA, and workers comp loads, the source you used to benchmark the starting wage, and the final loaded hourly figure.
fields.example: Benchmarked starting pay on Indeed before setting the wage; a PayScale report runs about $100 [Commercial Cleaning CEO — 598Td1ks52Y @ 00:04:22]. Base $15 plus state and federal unemployment, FICA and workers comp equals $17.71 an hour [Commercial Cleaning CEO — IMbK5m7qbY0 @ 00:04:42]. Every later step of the bid uses $17.71, never the raw $15 wage.

fields.name: full_cost_build
fields.prompt: Build the full monthly cost of the account line by line. Include labor hours at the loaded rate, supplies, equipment wear, overhead, and every forgotten site task such as keys, alarm codes, lock-up, restocking, and inspections before any margin math.
fields.example: Reference model for 10,000 sq ft, five nights: 86.6 labor hours at a $22.50 loaded rate, plus $225 supplies, $125 equipment wear and $350 overhead, totaling $2,650 [Janitorial Empire — PmZvMyhPjCM @ 00:03:49]. Added lines for keys, alarm codes, lock-up, restock checks and quality inspections before quoting [True Trade Cost — 8lFhFbsEuDc @ 00:01:49].

fields.name: margin_division_and_weeks
fields.prompt: Convert full cost into price by dividing by one minus your target margin, not by adding a markup. Show the weekly figure multiplied by 4.33 weeks, the target margin chosen, and the rounded monthly price that goes on the proposal.
fields.example: $2,650 divided by 0.75 is about $3,530, rounded to roughly $3,600 a month [Janitorial Empire — PmZvMyhPjCM @ 00:03:49]. Weekly pricing always uses 4.33 weeks: a $65 twice-weekly visit is $563 a month, not $520, recovering about $516 a year [Channel Zero Marketing — Ey7iPjW1uZQ @ 00:13:44]. Clean Proposals' 30% floor is noted for comparison.

fields.name: stress_test
fields.prompt: Stress-test the bid by adding one extra worker hour per visit and recalculating profit and margin. Record the original margin, the stressed margin, and whether the price still holds or must be revised before sending to the client.
fields.example: Reference case: a 20,000 sq ft, three-visit model priced at $2,800 moves from five to six worker hours per visit, cost rises to $2,425, profit drops to $375, and margin falls from 25% to about 13.4% [Bid & Profit Lab — T-l3Df3Iino @ 00:04:10]. My bid gets the same test before it leaves [Bid & Profit Lab — T-l3Df3Iino @ 00:04:26].

fields.name: deep_clean_and_scope_clause
fields.prompt: Price the initial deep clean as a separate one-off line and write the clause that reopens pricing when the client adds space or staff. Note the minimum visit charge you enforce on small jobs regardless of hourly math.
fields.example: Initial deep clean billed as its own one-time line; contract clause reopens the monthly price if the client adds space or staff, because scope creep is the silent margin killer [Solo Business Systems — hf0U17FyA58 @ 00:08:15]. Small visits carry a $65 floor whatever the hourly math says; price it like someone will be hired to work it [Channel Zero Marketing — Ey7iPjW1uZQ @ 00:22:36].

fields.name: cash_flow_reserve
fields.prompt: State the cash reserve you hold before chasing the next account, measured in months of the new account's costs. Record the payment terms you accepted, when the first payment realistically lands, and how payroll is covered meanwhile.
fields.example: Banked one full month of the new account's costs, about $2,650, before pursuing account two, because net 30 money lands around day 60 [Solo Business Systems — hf0U17FyA58 @ 00:09:25]. Following the rule to reject net 30 and net 60 terms and pay within 5 to 7 days of being paid [Commercial Cleaning CEO — o6xwPfuhTI4 @ 00:18:59].

fields.name: niche_target_selection
fields.prompt: Pick the high-profit niche you will target next and justify it. Name the client type, why it rewards stability, the compliance requirements crews must meet, and the margin range you expect compared with smaller accounts in your current book.
fields.example: Target: private medical offices, not hospitals; one company reached 97%+ medical revenue, about $550k a year, roughly one year in [Commercial Cleaning CEO — gqEvFieh5-k @ 00:02:15]. Compliance: bloodborne pathogen training, PPE and sharps handling for every crew member [nurselyf — Efj3Vo_qlBY @ 00:00:45]. Margin expectation for large accounts: 35-40% versus 50-60% on small [Commercial Cleaning CEO — -IxCGolievQ @ 00:21:40].

fields.name: day_porter_pricing
fields.prompt: Price a day porter position from hours, wage, and bill rate. Show daily hours, days per week, annual hours divided by twelve, the loaded bill rate, and confirm the bill rate clears wage plus load before the bid goes out.
fields.example: Four hours a day, five days, 10am-2pm: 1,040 hours a year divided by 12, rounded to 87 hours a month. An $18 wage loaded to a $26 bill rate gives $2,262 monthly [The Janitorial Store — 1c9Ty46MQbg @ 00:01:28]. Bidding $16 on a $15 wage would lose money every hour [OctoClean Media — 52I2LNERY3E @ 00:20:41].

fields.name: low_risk_proof_package
fields.prompt: List the proof you will include to look less risky to a large client. Cover communication speed, written SOPs, QC reporting, a custom never-miss checklist, background checks where required, and reporting for any new property manager who inherits the account.
fields.example: Being small is not the problem, looking risky is [Commercial Cleaning CEO — yfZUE5PZgvk @ 00:18:45]. Asked what one thing current cleaners always miss and built the never-miss checklist around it [Mike Mak — 92cY7nLDqTI @ 00:04:11]. Every new property manager gets a personal welcome with a historical snapshot report and a forward-looking report [Commercial Cleaning CEO — TCaVkVk94bc @ 00:08:10].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete when fixtures are counted as units, cost is fully loaded, price is divided by one minus margin at 4.33 weeks, the extra-hour stress test passes, one month of costs is banked, and the proof package is assembled.

worksheets.title: Public Bids and Post-Construction Pricing Worksheet
worksheets.purpose: Pressure-test your readiness for government janitorial bids and construction cleanup work by building cash reserves, compliance checklists, true-margin pricing, and phase-by-phase production math before any proposal or builder quote leaves your hands.
instructions: Start with the payroll float field; if you cannot fund payroll through slow public and builder payment cycles, stop before pricing anything.
Use measured square footage, tracked production rates, and loaded wages in every calculation rather than gut feel or a competitor's number.
Price public work by dividing total cost by one minus your target margin, never by adding a markup percentage to cost.
Read every solicitation and construction spec in full, noting mandatory site visits, submission formats, and buried extra cleans.
Keep the completed sheet in each bid file so pricing assumptions can be checked when the contract is awarded or audited.

fields.name: payroll_float_reserve
fields.prompt: Calculate the cash you need to float payroll before the first public or builder payment lands. Count net 30 to 60 terms, roughly 30 extra days for new vendors, and the crew size you would field on day one.
fields.example: Karen Denton warns you might pay employees before the customer pays you, so the gate is funding payroll for 10 employees first [Karen Denton KSC — xeZ8_Jlv0AI @ 00:01:44]. Darian Jarrett adds that net 30 can land closer to net 45 or 50 [Darian Jarrett — c9LRSgPQlvE @ 00:02:15]. Reserve target: 10-person payroll through day 60.

fields.name: public_contract_targets
fields.prompt: List the public contracts you will chase this quarter. For each, record where you found it, the contract end date, the agency, and why it fits your crew size, cash reserves, and past performance, plus which registration steps remain open.
fields.example: Sort FPDS by date signed and target contracts ending in 90 days to 4 months; Victoria Menifee surfaced a $27,000 embassy BPA exactly this way [victoria menifee — 5htVyehKCRo @ 00:46:54]. GovKidMethod notes not every contract requires past performance [GovKidMethod — dOj6rxt15uE @ 00:48:56], so a newer firm logs those first. Each row gets the end date and agency.

fields.name: site_visit_and_submission_check
fields.prompt: Before drafting any public bid, confirm mandatory site visit attendance, the exact submission format, the deadline, and every required form. Note which questions you will ask privately in person and which you will email to contracting, so nothing disqualifies the proposal.
fields.example: Non-attendees at a mandatory site visit are immediately rejected [Commercial Cleaning CEO — j4duUCt9Dlw @ 00:05:39]. Matt asked privately in the hallway how many staff the job should take and why it was rebid. Separately, one emailed question from Derek forced an amendment adding a pricing schedule the solicitation had omitted [GovKidMethod — dOj6rxt15uE @ 00:59:08].

fields.name: true_margin_monthly_price
fields.prompt: Build your monthly public-sector price by totaling labor, loaded payroll, supplies, transportation, and overhead, then dividing by one minus your target margin. Show the markup version beside it on paper so the gap between the two methods is visible.
fields.example: Small Business Bid School stresses a 20% margin is not the same as adding 20% to cost [Small Business Bid School — uARedcLLS5c @ 00:02:12]. Five nights at four hours, $22 an hour loaded 25%, plus $180 supplies, $120 transportation and $300 overhead, totals about $2,983; divided by 0.8, that becomes about $3,729 a month.

fields.name: sca_billable_hours
fields.prompt: For any federal service contract, record paid hours, billable hours, the health and welfare rate, and the vacation and holiday load from the wage determination. Explain how your labor line prices the gap between paid and billable time.
fields.example: GovKidMethod bills federal work off 1,920 billable hours out of 2,080 paid, because SCA wage determinations carry two weeks of vacation and two weeks of holidays [GovKidMethod — dr59GJ2T5v4 @ 00:43:54]. Skipping that gap has produced Department of Labor back-pay findings in the hundreds of thousands, so health and welfare get loaded too.

fields.name: workers_comp_activity_coding
fields.prompt: Map each crew activity on the bid to its workers comp class code, then model premium as payroll by class code times the state base rate times the carrier loss cost multiplier. Flag activities likely to shift at audit.
fields.example: Runjob Software notes the same laborer carries a different comp rate sweeping a floor than working on the 30th floor or 16 feet underground, and the annual audit trues up every underestimate [Runjob Software — 0pkOO_oVhN8 @ 00:01:23]. New York janitorial base rates ran $12.31 down to $3.03 in 2022 [The Coyle Group - Business Insurance — HSh0vcHYmUI @ 00:00:56].

fields.name: post_construction_spec_read
fields.prompt: Read the full construction cleaning spec and list every phase you are actually being asked to perform: rough, final, punch, touch-up, and trade cleans. Note buried extra cleans, window coverage, and who handles overspray on the glass.
fields.example: OctoClean warns that final only versus final, punch and trade clean language is where six-figure labor losses hide [OctoClean Media — 9TymiXPWhyY @ 00:10:13]. Ask the super whether the trade fixes overspray or the cleaner bills it as T&M. If windows went uncovered, get a signed waiver before scraping [The Janitorial Store — RNflg846cs4 @ 00:08:23].

fields.name: post_construction_price_build
fields.prompt: Price the construction cleanup from measured square footage and a tracked production rate. Record phase pricing per square foot, labor hours, crew size, and the conditions that push you up, such as dust, debris, windows, restrooms, and deadline pressure.
fields.example: Steve Hansen tracks finals at 150 square feet per hour, so 15,000 square feet becomes 100 labor hours [The Janitorial Store — gTK5pzrNCqg @ 00:01:23]. His bands run rough $0.10 to $0.15, final $0.15 to $0.30, touch-up $0.06 to $0.12. Mark Etherton prices on dust, debris, windows, restrooms and deadline pressure [Mark Etherton - The Millionaire Playbook — PG-8SEuPFQk @ 00:02:01].

fields.name: site_readiness_and_paperwork
fields.prompt: List the site conditions and paperwork you must confirm before quoting a builder: water, electrical power, dumpsters, a named site contact, plus your W9, general liability, and workers compensation proof ready to send the same day.
fields.example: Builders ask for a W9, general liability and workers compensation regardless [Darian Jarrett — _hqGinSApYg @ 00:08:14], and Construction Clean Partners says 99% will not work with you without comp. On the walkthrough, confirm water, power and dumpsters, because no water means hauling it in and no power can mean generators [The Janitorial Store — RNflg846cs4 @ 00:03:41].

fields.name: floor_care_addon_menu
fields.prompt: Design your specialty add-on menu for VCT strip-and-refinish, touch-ups, and subbed exterior work. Set a per-square-foot range, a job minimum, the adjustments for density and finish buildup, and the referral fee you keep on subcontracted work.
fields.example: OctoClean bills strip-and-refinish at 35 to 45 cents a square foot with a $450 minimum, even on a closet [OctoClean Media — X3MX2xOshA4 @ 00:05:33]. Darian Jarrett grew a $7,083 medical-office bid to roughly $9,000 through $75-per-hour touch-ups and a subbed pressure wash, keeping about 10 percent of the $917 sub [Darian Jarrett — c9LRSgPQlvE @ 00:13:19].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when payroll float is funded, site visit and submission requirements are confirmed, the bid is priced at a true margin with SCA hours and comp class codes loaded, and the construction spec, site utilities, and W9, liability, and comp packet are all verified.

worksheets.title: Systems Proof and Bloodborne Safety Worksheet
worksheets.purpose: Turn timekeeping, QR feedback, and inspection reporting into proof that wins bids, and lock in a bloodborne pathogen program covering spill response, sharps handling, waste routing, vaccination offers, and training records for every crew member.
instructions: Answer the growth blocker field before evaluating any platform, so software is chosen to solve a named problem rather than bought on impulse.
Describe each system as the client will experience it: what they see, when they receive it, and how it proves the work happened.
Write crew-facing language from the cleaner's point of view, leading with shifts, hours, and fewer interruptions off the clock.
Treat every blood, vomit, or unknown spill as infectious when completing the safety fields, and write steps a new hire could follow alone.
Review the safety and records fields every time turnover brings in a new group of cleaners.

fields.name: growth_blockers
fields.prompt: Before booking any software demo, write your top three growth blockers in plain language. Then ask your team the same question, record their answers word for word, and note where their list differs from yours and why.
fields.example: Swept advises writing the top three blockers, then asking the team and sitting through the awkward silence [Swept — lPuBkaocWL8 @ 00:04:22]. Michael Brown warns that people negotiate and research at length, finally buy the software, and never log in. Software is a tool like a mop and bucket; it fails if the mop water never changes.

fields.name: clock_in_verification
fields.prompt: Describe how cleaners will clock in and how you will verify they are physically on site. Specify geofencing, facial recognition, or schedule-based clock-ins, and explain which convenient shortcuts you will refuse because they break location verification.
fields.example: Janitorial Manager limits clock-ins to the geofence and uses facial recognition to eliminate buddy punching [Janitorial Manager — LFXytjdaxWA @ 00:01:17]. Swept cautions that text-message clock-in gives no idea where the cleaner physically is [Swept — W0BOiP7F_64 @ 00:26:03]. Clock in from the schedule tab so reminders like the every-other-Tuesday boardroom clean appear.

fields.name: crew_rollout_message
fields.prompt: Draft the opening of the all-hands meeting where you introduce timekeeping and geofencing to your crews. Lead with what is in it for them, such as more shifts and hours, and list the phrases you will avoid saying.
fields.example: Swept says never pitch the geofence as anti-theft tracking; open with more shifts, more hours and what is in it for them [Swept — lPuBkaocWL8 @ 00:20:30]. Service On Command frames in-app messaging as a way to communicate without bugging staff off the clock [Service On Command — CXVWaxMTpV0 @ 00:03:58]. Avoid: watching, catching, stealing.

fields.name: payroll_variance_review
fields.prompt: Set your pre-payroll review routine. State which variance report you run, the threshold that flags a shift, who corrects outliers, and the rule that nothing pays out until every flagged entry is fixed or explained in writing.
fields.example: Swept runs the 60-minute variance report before payroll and corrects outliers like a 96-hour shift before anything pays out [Swept — W0BOiP7F_64 @ 00:19:43]. Janitorial Manager adds that technology can reduce labor costs while making sure payroll is correct and people show up [Janitorial Manager — D60Eb-ryFyc @ 00:01:22]. Flag threshold: 60 minutes.

fields.name: qr_feedback_placement
fields.prompt: Map where QR feedback codes will go in each client facility. Choose spots where staff and the public actually notice issues, decide what the scan reports, and set who receives the nightly summary of scanned areas and service times.
fields.example: Matt stopped trusting a site manager's verbal all-clear and placed codes where staff see issues, so complaints arrive timestamped and located [Commercial Cleaning CEO — -DEX3b-m000 @ 00:09:13]. Janitorial Manager puts the business logo on every code and can send a nightly email listing scanned areas and service times [Janitorial Manager — NDvJAHP1GQo @ 00:03:25].

fields.name: inspection_reporting
fields.prompt: Define your inspection routine for each account: who inspects, how often, which checklist is used, and how the report reaches the customer. Explain how you will prove inspections happen rather than simply claiming they do in proposals.
fields.example: Swept emails the inspection report to the customer before the supervisor leaves the building, because sharing inspections is what proves you do them [Swept — W0BOiP7F_64 @ 00:18:13]. Modern Field Service adds that when bidding a medical office, the inspection trail is the thing that wins and keeps the contract [Modern Field Service — Y00vfNH19Q4 @ 00:01:19].

fields.name: system_led_sales_pitch
fields.prompt: Script the proof section of your next proposal. Describe the demo account you will load with the prospect's name, the client portal login, QR codes, and inspection samples, and state which price-only buyers you will knowingly let go.
fields.example: Swept's co-founder won 80% of contracts at premium prices by proving the app in the bid; the lost 20% were price-only buyers [Swept — O45aBb4kNlA @ 00:06:14]. Matt credits QR codes and a pre-built client login for a $200,000-a-year contract after losing a six-figure account without them [Commercial Cleaning CEO — -DEX3b-m000 @ 00:09:44].

fields.name: bbp_spill_protocol
fields.prompt: Write your step-by-step blood and unknown spill protocol for crews on every account. Include area lockout, PPE, sharps handling, absorbing, the disinfectant dilution, the wet dwell time, bagging, glove removal order, handwashing, and how the incident gets logged.
fields.example: Greg at OctoClean mixes 2 1/4 cups water with 1/4 cup 5.25% bleach for a 1:10 dilution and keeps the surface wet for three minutes [OctoClean Media — Z8hsIGjmi_c @ 00:00:59]. Open the biohazard bag first, then swap to fresh gloves before grabbing the clean disinfectant bottle [OctoClean Media — Z8hsIGjmi_c @ 00:02:57].

fields.name: sharps_and_waste_route
fields.prompt: Document how sharps are picked up, contained, and removed, and confirm the waste route for spent spill kits at each site. Name the container, the tools used, and who you call so nothing contaminated reaches the regular dumpster.
fields.example: Set the sharps container on the ground with the lid open before lifting the syringe, never holding container and needle together [MA Exec. Office of Labor and Workforce Development — 4xmWcKLIfmA @ 00:14:09]. Imperial Brady warns that kit bags tossed in the dumpster turn the whole dumpster into hazardous waste charged to the facility [Imperial Brady — tCz-yNw0WBo @ 00:08:08].

fields.name: bbp_training_and_records
fields.prompt: Plan annual bloodborne pathogen training for your actual turnover. Estimate how many people you will train each year, the course cost, the hepatitis B vaccine offer timeline, waiver handling, exposure follow-up, and how long records are kept.
fields.example: Keep It Clean sizes 100 employees at 200% turnover as 300 people trained a year, with the course under $30 [Keep It Clean — 8EjRhmcPsz0 @ 00:04:06]. Offer the free hepatitis B series by day 10 and keep training records with dates and attendee names for three years [Training Videos — AxPTARAhtdA @ 00:04:45].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when growth blockers are written by owner and team, clock-ins are location-verified, a variance review runs before every payroll, QR and inspection reports reach clients automatically, and the spill, sharps, waste, vaccine, and training-record procedures are written and assigned.

worksheets.title: Workforce Classification, Coverage, and Ownership Worksheet
worksheets.purpose: Classify every cleaner by control rather than paperwork, size insurance and bonding to your real headcount, and test any franchise, subcontract, or remote model against what you actually keep per hour and whether you truly own the contracts you service.
instructions: Fill in the classification fields person by person, judging each relationship by who controls schedules, supplies, uniforms, and training.
Bring the classification and insurance answers to an accountant or bookkeeper before adding the next helper or subcontractor.
Record actual quoted premiums and bond amounts rather than estimates, and note the date each quote was received.
Convert every franchise, subcontract, or remote package into dollars kept and true hours worked before judging it.
Revisit this sheet whenever headcount, contract ownership terms, or your crew model changes.

fields.name: classification_control_audit
fields.prompt: For every person who cleans for you, answer the control questions honestly: who sets the schedule, who supplies equipment and uniforms, who trains them, and whether they serve other clients. Record the resulting W2 or 1099 classification.
fields.example: Commercial Cleaning CEO puts it plainly: it is not about taxes, it is about control [Commercial Cleaning CEO — 9BXhBVRp_XU @ 00:03:59]. DJ The Boss adds that part-timers using your equipment and training are employees. A contractor doing business only with you is probably an employee [The Janitorial Store — YC2NrvVJqlg @ 00:03:13].

fields.name: misclassification_risk
fields.prompt: Identify the events most likely to trigger a classification audit in your business, such as a released worker filing for unemployment or an injured cleaner claiming comp. Estimate the exposure and name the accountant or bookkeeper reviewing it.
fields.example: The Janitorial Store ran 1099 labor for about a year until a laid-off employee claimed unemployment and the company paid a fine and penalties [The Janitorial Store — YC2NrvVJqlg @ 00:01:38]. UpFlip's operator paid a $12,000 misclassification fine, so settle classification with an accountant before the first helper starts [UpFlip — d4Iip7BHXwg @ 00:24:43].

fields.name: subcontractor_compliance
fields.prompt: If you use subcontractors, list the proof you collect from each before they start: current general liability, workers comp, and evidence of other clients. Describe how your checklists and job queue enforce quality without directing how they clean.
fields.example: Your policy covers you and your legal employees, not subs, so collect their liability and comp proof [The Professional Cleaner — DDLzG49aDvU @ 00:04:43]. Jon Margalit never hands contractors schedules, supplies, uniforms or how-to instructions; network contractors who follow the process get more work and the rest fall off naturally [Jon Margalit — 8gbn-TCd4l4 @ 00:04:15].

fields.name: insurance_stack
fields.prompt: List every policy you carry or need: general liability limits, workers comp, janitorial bond amount, and any add-on riders. Record the monthly or annual premium for each, and set your threshold for paying small damage claims out of pocket.
fields.example: The Professional Cleaner recommends $1,000,000 aggregate and $500,000 per occurrence general liability at $30 to $100 a month [The Professional Cleaner — DDLzG49aDvU @ 00:03:20], and would pay a $500 floor restoration personally because filing raises rates. For luxury homes, mentioning a fine-art rider during the walkthrough typically drew a response of how soon can you start.

fields.name: bond_sizing
fields.prompt: Choose your janitorial bond amount based on headcount and the properties you serve. Record the bond level, the annual premium quoted, and which prospects or contracts require it, and note when headcount growth will force a larger bond.
fields.example: Surety Bonds Direct quotes five employees at $150 a year for a $15,000 bond and $171 for $25,000 [Surety Bonds Direct — uMW_ZJMW0ZU @ 00:03:46]. Commercial firms with 10 employees pay $328 for a $50,000 bond and $547 for $150,000, typically choosing $50,000 up to $250,000 by property [Surety Bonds Direct — uMW_ZJMW0ZU @ 00:04:12].

fields.name: w2_positioning
fields.prompt: Decide how your crew model shows up in proposals. If you run W2 crews, write the sentence you will use when buyers ask about 1099 versus W2, and explain how that choice supports brand control and retention.
fields.example: Commercial Cleaning CEO reviewed past proposals and found clients who asked about 1099 versus W2 consistently reacted with excitement to hearing the crew was W2 [Commercial Cleaning CEO — 9BXhBVRp_XU @ 00:10:06]. Draft line: every cleaner on your site is our W2 employee, trained, background-checked and covered by our workers comp.

fields.name: franchise_fee_stack
fields.prompt: If you are weighing a unit franchise, list every fee: royalty, marketing, admin and collection, insurance, and the finder fee per new account. Convert the stack into a percentage of billing and the dollars you actually keep.
fields.example: Commercial Cleaning CEO stacks royalty near 10 percent, marketing 2 to 10, and admin and collection 5 to 10 into 20 to 35 percent, sometimes 40, so $1,000 billed nets $600 to $800 [Commercial Cleaning CEO — xqw9zag57Uk @ 00:05:18]. Mike Mak paid four times monthly value per new account [Mike Mak — 6MDrTK46_8g @ 00:04:31].

fields.name: effective_hourly_wage
fields.prompt: Convert any franchise or subcontract package into a true hourly wage. Divide the post-fee monthly payout by the hours you would honestly work, then compare it against the $16 to $30 range the account should have paid.
fields.example: Clean For A Dream shows a $705 monthly payout on a five-night account that should take 24 to 44 hours, yet franchisees actually work about 100 hours, roughly $7 an hour [Clean For A Dream — fs86ZhCBfJ8 @ 00:51:00]. Ben Bragg says the franchising industry is designed to supplement income, not create owners.

fields.name: contract_ownership_check
fields.prompt: Confirm who owns each customer contract you service. Note whether a franchisor or prime can reassign accounts when the customer is happy, what new accounts cost, and the two questions you will ask before signing anything.
fields.example: AJ Simmons describes walking away with pretty much nothing after fees and underbidding, feeling like a glorified employee [AJ SIMMONS — Bbay8f0-XFM @ 00:03:28]. Win Driggins puts it simply: the hidden business is the contract itself. Mike Mak asks what the support fees are and what a new account costs [Mike Mak — 6MDrTK46_8g @ 00:06:32].

fields.name: remote_model_math
fields.prompt: If you are considering a remote or laptop-run model, rerun the per-job math with real acquisition cost, card fees, software, insurance, refunds, and recleans. Compare the net per job against a commercial contract alternative before scaling into hundreds of jobs.
fields.example: Mike Mak shows a $225 clean leaving a $90 owner split that shrinks to about $30 after $40 to $50 acquisition, card fees, software, insurance, refunds and recleans [Mike Mak — kbRmM3sctgA @ 00:03:13]. Logan Robison charges new short-term rental hosts a $150 onboarding fee plus a mandatory deep clean [Logan Robison — mrd8LK8fcFM @ 00:25:24].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when every cleaner is classified by control and reviewed by an accountant, sub liability and comp proof is on file, insurance and bond premiums are recorded from real quotes, and any franchise, subcontract, or remote model is converted to dollars kept, true hourly pay, and confirmed contract ownership.
